title: Drift-audit records carry {ruleId, outcome, timestamp, diff} (no clientIpHash); request-event records carry {ruleId, clientIpHash, outcome, timestamp} on the runtime path, hashed prefix only
asA: operator on the applying project reading drift-audit reports and rate-limit event records through the applied logging companion
iWant: the drift-audit runner to emit records without clientIpHash (no client on the API path) and the runtime request-event path to emit records with a clientIpHash hashed prefix only; both classes never carry a full client IP, never a request body, never a user agent
soThat: the audit trail is safe to store, forward and read without additional PII scrubbing at the audit sink

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a synthetic drift-audit payload constructed from a fixture rule and a fake live-zone response, and a separate runtime request-event synthetic payload, when the event-secrecy probe reads the sink, every drift-audit record carries only {ruleId, outcome, timestamp, diff} (never clientIpHash, never a full IP as regex 4-octet dotted quad or v6 group, never a request-body key, never a user-agent key), and every request-event record carries only {ruleId, clientIpHash, outcome, timestamp} where clientIpHash is a bounded hashed prefix (32 hex chars max, never a full IP); the probe returns aggregateVerdict:pass.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the shipped drift-audit runner and a synthetic input pair
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event-secrecy probe drives the runner and inspects the resulting records
acceptanceCriteria.then: every record carries only the metadata-safe fields; SIMULATE_EVENT_LEAK_IP=true surfaces a leaked key and the aggregate verdict is fail

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the SIMULATE_EVENT_LEAK_IP=true switch, a full IP is injected into a record produced by the runner, when the event-secrecy probe reads the sink, the probe returns aggregateVerdict:fail with detail naming the leaked key.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the drift-audit runner producing records under SIMULATE_EVENT_LEAK_IP=true (a full IP injected into one record)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event-secrecy probe scans the sink
acceptanceCriteria.then: the probe returns aggregateVerdict:fail with detail naming the leaked key
